default: Use the native runtime MCP client with an existing maintained provider MCP server for external service connectors.
customTools: Review existing custom tools, plugins and service API wrappers for equivalent MCP capabilities. Migrate active consumers and retire redundant implementations after actual native consumption succeeds.
selection: Prefer the service provider's maintained MCP server and documented native installation/authentication.
Select capabilities for the actual Project/Work and profile; do not enable every connector in every profile.
Distinguish configured, exposed, authenticated and behaviorally verified capabilities.
Keep native lifecycle, credentials, permissions and tool discovery with Codex or Hermes.
replacement: Verify capability coverage, current consumers, required account/scopes and actual native behavior.
Preserve original bytes and completed effects, switch consumers, then remove the exact redundant custom entrypoint.
For a required function absent from MCP, record the gap and retain the smallest supported official/native operation until coverage exists.
Do not add a custom MCP bridge around the old API merely to rename its transport.
retainedMeaning: Project/Work/Issue/Spec/Plan identities and actual user decisions
Source bytes, provenance, evidence and common checkpoint CAS
Native product APIs, local computation and official runtime tools

nativeOwnership.codex: Native MCP configuration, client, tool catalog, authentication and session lifecycle
nativeOwnership.hermes: Native profile MCP configuration, client, process connection pools, authentication and session lifecycle
nativeOwnership.common: Connector selection and migration meaning only; no second client, registry, scheduler or credential store

scope: Only admitted Work and custom integrations; excluded domains and vendor/builtin skills remain outside migration scope.
